conditions: It is a team in Linear (not a project, issue, or other entity).
The team's visibility is private (as opposed to a public team).
The team's key starts with the letters "GR".
The team's description contains language referring to "the Q3 OKR pilot rollout".
The action to perform is renaming the team's name to "Growth Pod" (the display name, not the key).
There is exactly one team matching all of the above (the request uses "the," implying uniqueness).

ambiguities.phrase: whose description mentions the Q3 OKR pilot rollout
readings: The description contains that exact phrase or something very close to it.
The description merely references that general topic/initiative using different wording (e.g., "OKR pilot for Q3" or "the rollout of Q3 OKR pilots").
Q3 of some other year (e.g., 2025) if the description specifies a different year.
Case-sensitive match on the literal key string (Linear keys are conventionally uppercase).

records.note: Private team, key GRW starts with GR, and description explicitly reads 'Coordinates the Q3 OKR pilot rollout across regional sales teams.' Matches all three conditions and is the unique match.
Private (true) and key GRO starts with GR, but its description is about internal tooling/support, with no mention of the Q3 OKR pilot rollout.
Key GRA starts with GR and description matches the Q3 OKR pilot rollout text exactly, but private is false, so it is a public team, not a private one.
Private and description matches, but its key is PTN, which does not start with GR (only its name, 'Growth Partnerships', starts with 'Growth').
Public team, key ENG does not start with GR, and description is unrelated to the Q3 OKR pilot rollout.
Private team, but key SLS does not start with GR and description is about sales pipeline, not the Q3 OKR pilot rollout.

turn2.differences: The author's three conditions (c1-c3) match my step-1 reading closely. They omit stating explicitly that the target must be a 'team' entity and that the match should be unique, but both are trivially implied by the phrasing and hold in the data (t-growth is the only team satisfying all three conditions).

ambiguity_effects.phrase: whose description mentions the Q3 OKR pilot rollout
ambiguity_effects.explain: In the abstract, 'mentions' could mean an exact phrase match or a looser topical reference. In this dataset it doesn't matter: the teams with matching descriptions (t-growth, t-growthanalytics, t-growthpartnerships) all use the identical exact phrase, and the non-matching teams (t-growthops, t-eng, t-sales) have descriptions with no relation to Q3 OKR pilots under either reading, so the two readings select the same set of candidates.

No year is specified, so in principle 'Q3' could refer to different fiscal years. But no team description in the data mentions any year at all, so this ambiguity has no bearing on which record is selected.
All team keys in the data are uppercase (GRW, GRO, GRA, PTN, ENG, SLS), matching Linear's convention, so case sensitivity is not a live concern and doesn't affect the outcome.

turn2.naturalness_note: The request is more specific than typical casual phrasing (naming the key prefix and quoting description content rather than just saying 'the Growth team'), but this specificity is well-motivated here: there are multiple similarly-named 'Growth...' teams with overlapping descriptions, so a user familiar with this workspace disambiguating by key and description content reads as plausible rather than artificial.
